units.text: INT. SHUTTERED CAROUSEL FACTORY - NIGHT
A cavernous workshop under a rusted skylight.
Painted horses hang from chains, half-carved, half-gilded, their glass eyes catching the moon.
Sawdust drifts like old snow.
A single bare bulb swings over a workbench.
INEZ MARQUARDT, 40s, a detective in a wet raincoat, leans against a pillar.
Her hair is tied back with a rubber band.
Her face is calm, but her fingers drum.
CARMINE, 50s, a carver with a chisel scar across his left cheek, sits at the bench with a half-finished stallion.
He is huge and slow and gentle.
DOROTHEA, 60s, the factory's owner, stands in the doorway of a glass-walled office, a cigarette burning down in her hand.
VLAD, 30s, her nephew, lurks at her shoulder in a leather jacket.
REGGIE, 20s, a rawboned kid in a yellow slicker, hovers near the big double doors as if ready to run.
Inez takes her time.
She walks along the line of hanging horses.
She touches one.
It swings.
She doesn't look at him when she speaks.
He says you knew the girl.
units.name: INEZ

units.text: He says a lot.
units.name: CARMINE

units.text: He says you carved her a pony.
units.name: INEZ

units.text: He says that.
units.name: CARMINE

units.text: Did you?
units.name: INEZ

units.text: Carmine turns the chisel over in his hands.
He looks at it, not at her.
She liked the grey ones.
units.name: CARMINE

units.text: She's been missing nine days.
units.name: INEZ

units.text: It's a long time.
units.name: CARMINE

units.text: Dorothea steps out of the office.
Her heels click on the concrete.
She draws on the cigarette and exhales a long, thin line of smoke.
Detective, my carver is a gentle man. He works. He eats. He goes home.
units.name: DOROTHEA

units.text: Where's home?
units.name: INEZ

units.text: Upstairs.
units.name: DOROTHEA

units.text: In this building?
units.name: INEZ

units.text: He has no other.
units.name: DOROTHEA

units.text: Vlad shifts.
His boots scuff.
He shoves his hands into his jacket pockets, then pulls them out again.
Inez notices.
She says nothing.
She walks to the bench.
Looks at the stallion, then at Carmine's hands.
Then she picks up a small grey pony, perfect, half-finished, from the shavings.
She holds it up to the light.
A tiny name is carved on its belly.
"For Wren."
units.name: INEZ

units.text: Silence.
Nobody breathes.
The bulb swings.
Reggie bolts for the double doors.
Hauls one open.
Rain pours in.
He is through, running, the yellow slicker vanishing into the dark.
Vlad lunges after him.
Dorothea screams his name.

Inez drops the pony and draws her revolver in one smooth move, but Carmine is already on his feet, huge, quiet, between her and the door, the chisel hanging at his side like a thing he's forgotten he's holding.
Not the boy.
units.name: CARMINE

units.text: Inez does not lower the gun.
She does not fire.
Where is she, Carmine?
units.name: INEZ

units.text: He tilts his head toward the ceiling.
Up, past the beams, to a trapdoor in the rafters.
A rope ladder hangs, swaying.
She's been waiting for her pony.
units.name: CARMINE

units.text: Inez lowers the gun an inch.
She looks at the ladder.
She looks at the grey pony on the floor.
And she begins to climb.
